John McEnroe. An American tennis champion who won seven Grand Slam singles titles and dominated the 1980s with a serve-and-volley game and unprecedented volatility on court. His passionate intensity, legendary disputes with umpires, and rivalry with Björn Borg defined an era and made him one of tennis's most memorable and captivating figures. He won four US Opens between 1979 and 1981, and again in 1984, establishing the tournament as his signature venue. He also won three Wimbledons in 1981, 1983, and 1984, cementing his place among the era's greatest players. Known for his serve-and-volley game, superior court sense, and especially his left-handed serve which was nearly unreturnable to most opponents, he dominated the net. He is infamous for his on-court tantrums, animated arguments with umpires, and the phrase "You cannot be serious," which became his defining catchphrase and part of tennis folklore. He reached world number one in 1983 and held the ranking for 170 weeks, with his competitive peak spanning the late 1970s through mid-1980s. He played doubles successfully, winning sixteen Grand Slam titles in men's doubles and mixed doubles combined. The 1980 Wimbledon final against Björn Borg, which he lost six to eight, five to seven, six to three, seven to six, six to four, remains one of the most celebrated and memorable matches ever played in professional tennis.
